title: Design Signals: usage gallery and progressive migration plan for tokens, controls, and data surfaces
creator: Ava Martin
description: Create a compact, example-driven documentation gallery ("Design Signals") that consolidates usage guidance, API examples, and stepwise migration notes for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts. The goal is to reduce ambiguity for engineers and designers when upgrading components or replacing legacy token names, and to provide a lightweight reference that complements the full component API pages.
background: We have multiple scattered docs and a lot of implicit conventions about token semantics (primary/secondary/interactive states), button sizing and accessibility rules, table column patterns, and chart color theming. Teams keep opening tickets asking for explicit do/don't examples and migration knobs. Recent migration of tokens in runtime-1.18 surfaced several edge-cases (icon-only buttons, dense table rows, and stacked charts) that weren't captured in the canonical docs.
proposal: Ship a newDocs 'Design Signals' section under the components area with the following parts: (1) a visual usage gallery with succinct captions and code snippets for common variants; (2) a migration checklist per surface (tokens → new tokens mapping, button props to prefer, table API changes if any, chart theme keys); (3) API quick-reference cards (props, accessibility notes); and (4) a short 'regression test prompts' list teams can copy into their eval harness. Keep each page compact (~250-400 words) plus 3–5 curated examples.
migration_notes:
- Tokens: include explicit mapping table (oldToken -> newToken) and recommended fallback rules for runtime compatibility.
- Buttons: call out edge-case for icon-only states (maintain 44px hit area) and replacement for legacy size tokens.
- Tables: document stable column key pattern and how to migrate sorting/accessibility hooks.
- Charts: map legacy chart palette tokens to new theme keys and list steps to opt into auto-contrast in releases prior to chart-2025.06.
examples: Tokens: code snippet showing color tokens for interactive state with a short caption — best: use 'token.interactive.primary' rather than raw hex; avoid hard-coding colors in components.
Button: small, medium, large variants with icon-only example. Show ARIA attributes and min-hit area enforcement. Include recommended prop: 'size: `md`' + 'accessible: true'.
Table: column API example with stable 'id' keys, explicit cell renderers, and a small accessibility example for screen-reader-only headers.
Charts: thematic example switching from 'legacyBlue' -> 'brand.primary' and the snippet to enable 'autoContrast: true' for label legibility.
do_dont: Do: prefer semantic tokens (e.g., token.surface.card) in component styles so runtime can remap them during client migrations.
Do: include one failing visual regression snapshot for each example variant in the PR.
Don't: hardcode spacing or color hexes in component logic — use the tokens layer.
Don't: assume table row heights are fixed; prefer density tokens and let teams override at the page level.
acceptance_criteria: A concise 'Design Signals' landing page exists with links to four leaf pages: Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts.
Each leaf page contains: at least 3 curated examples, one migration checklist, one API quick-reference card, and accessibility notes.
Design and engineering have approved the code snippets (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234).
Docs pass review checklist and a short usability check with two internal teams (Prod and Growth).
A migration gist mapping old->new tokens is published and linked from the tokens page.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft content and Figma gallery (Priya) + initial engineering stub for code snippets.
Week 2: Cross-team review (UX, Accessibility, Runtime) + iterate examples and migration checklist.
Week 3: Final edits, merge PR to docs site, and announce in #design and weekly all-hands digest.
Optional: host a 30-min office hours for two weeks after release to answer migration questions.
notes: Trade-offs: keeping examples minimal reduces surface area but may omit some rare variants; we prefer adding follow-up micro-guides for niche patterns.
Decision: use semantic token names as the single source of truth for examples to avoid repeating raw values.
Controllers: propose adding a small 'migration helper' script for infra teams later (tracked separately).
